title: Naive Bayes for numbers and for words
brief: Fit Gaussian naive Bayes with per-class variances, fit a smoothed word-count model, and score documents by summing count times log word probability.
hints: For each class, X[y == k].mean(axis=0) and X[y == k].var(axis=0) give the per-feature mean and variance. np.var divides by the class count by default, which is what you want. Apply np.maximum(variance, var_floor).
For the word model, sum the count rows of a class first, then add alpha to every word, then divide by that smoothed total. The log of the result is one row of log_theta.

A document's score for a class is counts @ log_theta[k] + log_priors[k]. For all classes at once that is X @ log_theta.T + log_priors, an (n, K) array. Subtract log_sum_exp(joint, axis=1) as a column.
